intent: Surface the loop kill-switch in session status so an agent inside a checkout can see it. The switch lives on the loop-control branch, never in the working tree, so the obvious local existence check always reports absent -- an agent worked a full day against an ENGAGED switch on that reading. The probe reads the local remote-tracking ref only (read-only, no network) and reports UNKNOWN rather than CLEAR when the ref cannot be read.

commit.message: fix(onboard): show the loop kill-switch in session status

interface_mismatches: Six guarded workflows resolve the kill-switch against the loop-control branch via the GitHub contents API, while an agent inside a checkout has only the working tree, where the file is never present. The two surfaces answered different questions and only the workflows' answer was correct.
honest_blockers: The reading is a local remote-tracking ref only. A stale or unfetched ref cannot see a switch engaged after the last fetch; that case reports UNKNOWN with its own refresh command rather than CLEAR, but UNKNOWN is still weaker than the workflows' live query and is not a substitute for it.
This changes only what a session can SEE. It does not gate anything: no edit, merge, or push is blocked by the reading, and an agent that ignores an ENGAGED line is still unimpeded by this change.
Verified against one engaged switch and synthetic clones. No test exercises a switch that is engaged and then cleared mid-session.

Track attribution is a judgement, not a fact: no ACTIVE track owns dharma_swarm/operator_core/onboarding/ since onboard-one-door-2026-07 retired. repository-titanium-hardening-2026-07 is claimed on theme (truthful verification) and because it owns the onboarding contract test that caught the first attempt. The operator may reassign.

CEREMONY ORDER WAS VIOLATED AND THE RECEIPT DOES NOT SHOW IT. The code was authored and committed before this packet existed; the branch was then rewound to base_ref so preflight could bind. The resulting binding receipt therefore attests that the diff CONFORMS to the declared scope, not that scope was declared first. Read the closeout as a scope-conformance check only.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the module, the two onboarding wirings, the tests, and this packet together. Session status returns to not mentioning the kill-switch; the workflows' own guards are untouched throughout.
